wineries.name: Stone Tower Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Hilltop estate with panoramic Blue Ridge views and a serious wine program.
wineries.editorial: Stone Tower sits on Hogback Mountain at the western edge of Loudoun. Two sides to the property: the polished Tower View Tasting Room (21+ club) and the casual, all-ages Harvest Barn. Both share the view that justifies the drive.
policyNotes: Outside food NOT permitted — both tasting rooms have food menus
Leashed dogs welcome inside and outside Harvest Barn; outside Tower View only
Harvest Barn: family-friendly, all ages, walk-in (no reservations for groups of 8 or fewer)
Max 2.5-hour visit per party in public spaces

wineries.name: Bluemont Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 951 feet up — arguably the best view in Virginia wine country.
wineries.editorial: Bluemont's elevation is its whole pitch and it delivers. The patio looks east over the Loudoun Valley toward DC on a clear day. Bring a sweater in any season; the wind up here has opinions.
policyNotes: Outside food and beverage explicitly prohibited — Virginia ABC regulations cited
Dogs welcome: inside tasting room + panoramic terrace; leashed required
Food available on site: boards, flatbread, brunch weekends
Live music Saturdays ~3:30–6:30 PM (Sunset Saturdays); occasional Friday member events
Credit card required for reservations; $10/person no-show fee

wineries.name: Breaux Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Sprawling Cajun-influenced estate, the most-awarded vineyard in Virginia.
wineries.editorial: Breaux is big — over 100 acres planted — and the experience matches the scale. Stretch out on the lawn, order the muffuletta from the kitchen, and work through the Nebbiolo or the Viognier.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome leashed outdoors (EXCEPT Orleans Patio); also inside Vin 97 tasting room
Outside food permitted outdoors only; NOT inside tasting room
Groups 8+ must use picnic grounds, not patio
No outside alcohol of any kind — Breaux wine only
Kitchen open daily 11 AM–5 PM; gourmet light fare and freshly baked bread
Guided tastings require reservation; only 2 per day accepted

wineries.name: Lost Mountain Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Appointment-only Bordeaux-style cellar (formerly RdV) — widely regarded as Virginia's best producer.
wineries.editorial: Lost Mountain Vineyards is the new chapter of what was RdV Vineyards — same hillside in Delaplane, same Bordeaux-style ambition, new name. A proper appointment: book a ~90-minute experience, taste through the flagship blends, leave understanding why people compare Virginia to Bordeaux on its best days.
policyNotes: Rebranded from RdV Vineyards in 2026 — same property, new name
By appointment ONLY — no walk-ins; reservations via Tock
Hillside vineyard with Blue Ridge views

wineries.name: Barboursville Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Italian-owned estate surrounding Jefferson-designed ruins. Iconic.
wineries.editorial: The Zonin family bought this property in 1976 and have been making serious Bordeaux and Italian varietals here ever since. Walk the ruins of Governor Barbour's Jefferson-designed mansion, eat at Palladio restaurant, taste through the Octagon.
policyNotes: No outside food in tasting room — seasonal charcuterie/cheese available on site
Dogs leashed in main tasting room ONLY — NOT in Library tasting room or inside buildings generally
Palladio Restaurant on site: fine dining; lunch Wed–Sun, dinner Fri–Sat (reservation required)
Historic estate: ruins of 1814 Barboursville Mansion on grounds

wineries.name: King Family Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Polo matches Sunday afternoons, world-class Meritage all year.
wineries.editorial: King Family hits every note of the modern Virginia winery: serious wine program (the Meritage is the flagship), gorgeous outdoor lawn, food trucks on weekends, and Sunday polo matches in season.
policyNotes: BYO food welcome; no outside alcohol
Shop: local cheeses, charcuterie, baguettes, crackers, preserves, nuts
Polo Sundays: Memorial Day weekend through mid-October (weather/field permitting)

wineries.name: Veritas Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Blue Ridge backdrop and a full kitchen for sit-down lunch with the wine.
wineries.editorial: Veritas is dialed in — the wines are good, the views are great, and the Terrace serves real lunch (sandwiches, salads, charcuterie) until 4:30pm. The Farmhouse next door is a B&B if you want to make it a weekend.
policyNotes: BYO picnic permitted in Bricks outdoor area; order wine at bar
Dogs welcome leashed on lawn and veranda; NOT inside tasting room
Food menu on site: shareable items indoors and outdoors
Live music: Starry Nights Summer Music Series + special events throughout year

wineries.name: Early Mountain Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Steve Case's flagship — sophisticated wood-fired food, focused tastings.
wineries.editorial: Early Mountain is the most thoughtfully designed tasting room in Virginia. The food matches the wine, the seasonal Meadow is enormous, and the tasting flights are well-curated for someone trying to understand Virginia for the first time.
policyNotes: Outside food NOT permitted — licensed as a restaurant
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; water bowls and treats provided
Thu–Mon only; closed Tue–Wed; weekend hours vary for private events

wineries.name: Pearmund Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: One of Virginia's oldest Chardonnay vineyards, walk-in friendly.
wineries.editorial: Pearmund is unfussy. The vineyard's older Chardonnay vines produce one of the best whites in the state. The main winery is adults-only; families head to the Pearmund Farmstore next door.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome on leash outdoors; cleanup required
Food platters available: meats, cheeses, nuts, dips, chocolates
Daily 10 AM–6 PM; Fridays until 8 PM
Main winery is 21+ only; Farmstore location is family-friendly

wineries.name: Greenhill Winery & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Middleburg estate. Adults-only, sparkling-strong, all-day Mezze menu.
wineries.editorial: Greenhill is the rare Virginia winery that pulls off elegant without being stuffy. The Blanc de Blancs is the bottle to know. The Mezze menu (cheeses, charcuterie, caviar) plays nicely with whatever you're drinking. Strict 21+ throughout — leave the kids and infants at home.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome in outdoor areas; leash required
No outside food inside tasting room (outdoor BYO policy not explicitly stated — verify)
On-site Mezze Menu: cheeses, charcuterie, bread, caviar; self-serve accoutrement bar

wineries.name: Chrysalis Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Norton specialists — America's native grape, taken seriously.
wineries.editorial: Chrysalis planted the largest Norton vineyard in the world here. If you've never tried Virginia's native grape, this is the place to start. The onsite Little River Bakehouse serves pizza, paninis, and salads alongside the wine.
policyNotes: Outside food and beverages NOT permitted
Dogs leashed in outdoor areas ONLY — commercial kitchen and cheese creamery require VDACS animal exclusion indoors
Food on site: pizza (Little River Bakehouse), Locksley Farmstead artisan cheese, crackers, dips, spreads
Last food/beverage call 30 min before close
Closed New Year's Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas; 5 PM close Dec 24 and 31

wineries.name: Ingleside Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Tidewater estate, fourth-generation family, picnic-perfect courtyard.
wineries.editorial: Ingleside is a drive from DC but worth the day. The Tidewater terroir produces wines unlike anywhere else in Virginia. The European-style courtyard with the fountain is the picnic spot of the trip.
policyNotes: Gourmet cheeses and sausages available for purchase
Summer Music Series: live music on patio during summer

wineries.name: Linden Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A quiet, terroir-obsessed mountainside winery for serious wine drinkers who want to think and not perform.
wineries.editorial: Linden is the rare Virginia winery that treats tasting as an intellectual exercise — vintages and vineyard sites compared side by side, with founder Jim Law's fingerprints on every pour. The view is gorgeous, but the policies (no kids, no pets, no groups over four) make it clear this is a place to slow down rather than party. Bring your own picnic to enjoy on the deck after you taste, and you'll see why the wine cognoscenti consider this the soul of Virginia wine.
policyNotes: Adults only (21+) — no guests under 21 including infants
Maximum 4 people per reservation; no combining reservations
Outside food permitted after tasting (indoor/outdoor distinction not specified on site)
Tastings focus on terroir, vintage, and vineyard site comparison — educational format

wineries.name: The Winery at La Grange
wineries.vibeDescriptor: An 18th-century manor-house winery just outside DC where weekend afternoons mean live music, picnics, and Virginia reds.
wineries.editorial: La Grange has a restored stone manor at its center, picnic tables on the lawn, and weekend live music that turns it into the closest thing to a true wine-country day trip from the DC suburbs. They sell cheese, hummus, baguettes, and spreads to enhance your visit, but they also actively welcome you to bring your own picnic — a real rarity. Dogs on leashes are good outside; service dogs only inside the manor.
policyNotes: BYO food welcome in outdoor areas
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; NOT inside historic manor house (service dogs only inside)
On-site: artisan cheeses, gourmet meats, bread, crackers — individually packaged

wineries.name: Boxwood Estate Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A polished, French-inspired estate where Middleburg horse country meets Bordeaux-style blends served from a chic stone courtyard.
wineries.editorial: Boxwood is 100% estate, hyper-focused on Bordeaux varieties, and the experience matches — a beautiful tasting room, a Chai (French cellar), and a courtyard with fire tables under a giant river birch. It's strictly 21+, no pets, no outside food beyond a birthday cake, which keeps the vibe more wine-bar-in-the-vineyard than picnic-blanket-Saturday. Reserve a table for weekends; walk-ins are welcome but the space is intimate.
policyNotes: Pets NOT permitted anywhere on property
Outside food prohibited (exception: birthday cakes/cupcakes only)
Food available on site: cheese boards, charcuterie, hummus, sandwiches
Smoke-free inside; designated smoking area in parking lot
Reservations encouraged; groups 6+ book Group Tasting Experience

wineries.name: Michael Shaps Wineworks
wineries.vibeDescriptor: A no-nonsense Charlottesville winery from a Burgundy-trained vet pouring both his Virginia wines and imported Maison Shaps Burgundies.
wineries.editorial: Michael Shaps is the closest you'll get in Virginia to a proper Burgundy domaine — he literally makes wine in both places. The tasting room is relaxed and dog-friendly, with a big deck, stone patio, and front lawn where picnicking is encouraged; cheese and baguettes are sold inside if you didn't bring your own. Open daily, walk-ins welcome, and a quieter alternative to the busier C'ville-area names.
policyNotes: BYO food permitted outdoors — picnicking on lawn/patio encouraged
Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; must clean up
Cheese and charcuterie plates available; food trucks on select days

wineries.name: The Winery at Bull Run
wineries.vibeDescriptor: The closest proper Virginia farm winery to DC — festive, social, BYO picnic on the lawn.
wineries.editorial: The closest proper Virginia farm winery to Washington DC, Bull Run sits on historic Civil War-era land in Centreville with a split personality: an adult-only front lawn and a family-friendly back area with food trucks and live music every Fri/Sat/Sun. BYO picnics are welcome on the outdoor lawn (not indoors or covered patios), and Bull Run Pizza is on-site almost every day. It skews festive and social rather than intimate — expect weekend crowds and easy parking off Lee Highway.
policyNotes: BYO food permitted on outdoor lawn tables only — NOT indoors or on covered patios
Soft coolers, picnic baskets, lunch boxes with ice packs OK; hard coolers prohibited
No outside beverages of any kind (ABC Farm Winery License)
Dogs in Dog-Park section ONLY — not in tasting room, at bars, on patios, or public lawns
21+ zone: front lawn and covered patio; family zone: back lawn and tent (children supervised)
Live music every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday
Food trucks Sat–Sun year-round; Fri evenings in spring/summer
Walk-in only since Oct 2022; groups 13+ need 24-hour advance notice

wineries.name: Paradise Springs Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Rare Fairfax-proper winery — wine country without the 45-minute drive west.
wineries.editorial: Tucked into the wooded hills of Clifton, Paradise Springs is one of the very few wineries within Fairfax County itself — a rare find for Northern Virginia residents who want wine country without the 45-minute drive. The estate grows its own fruit and offers extended Friday evenings alongside a seven-day schedule that outpaces most Loudoun competitors.
policyNotes: BYO food permitted outdoors (lawn) with minimal restrictions; no grills or tent setups
BYO food indoors/back deck: must fit on your table; no coolers indoors or on back deck
No outside beverages of any kind — including no solid-colored plastic cups
Dogs welcome on lawn only with leash — NOT inside buildings or on back deck
Back patio deck is 21+ adults-only zone; children welcome on lawn and elsewhere with parents
Live music every Saturday and Sunday 1 PM–5 PM — free with purchase
Food Artisan Truck: Thu 4–6:30 PM, Fri 2–8:30 PM, Sat–Sun 11 AM–6:30 PM
No reservations Mon–Fri; weekend group tastings (1–20) require advance booking

wineries.name: Cana Vineyards and Winery of Middleburg
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 43-acre Middleburg AVA family farm — estate Viognier in a quiet rural setting.
wineries.editorial: A family farm winery on 43 acres of rolling Loudoun hills between Middleburg and Aldie, Cana has long been known for estate-grown Viognier and a quiet rural setting. As of April 2026 the property is officially listed for sale at $9M — it remains open while the transition plays out, but status could change. Call ahead before making the drive.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome leashed on ground floor, Sunset Pavilion, and grounds; treats + water bowls provided
BYO food welcome; food trucks also available on site
Second floor is 21+ only; ground level is family-friendly

wineries.name: 50 West Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Strictly 21+ across the property — quietly adult Middleburg AVA pick.
wineries.editorial: Set on 55 acres just east of Middleburg, 50 West enforces one of the stricter age policies in Northern Virginia wine country — the entire property is 21+, no children. That keeps the atmosphere notably quieter and more adult-focused than many Loudoun neighbors. Weekend live music and outdoor picnicking make it a reliable date-night or small-group destination.
policyNotes: 21+ ONLY — applies to entire property including all outdoor spaces
BYO food/non-alcoholic beverages permitted outdoors; coolers inspected; no outside food indoors
Dogs leashed in outdoor areas main level only — not inside tasting room
Decorative items require event rental or will be returned to vehicle

wineries.name: 8 Chains North
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Off-leash dog park, a real food menu, and a permissive BYO policy — Loudoun's most all-in winery.
wineries.editorial: One of the most family- and dog-friendly wineries in Loudoun County, 8 Chains North in Waterford features an off-leash dog park, a full food menu, and a genuinely permissive outside food policy. Extended Wednesday evenings and late Friday hours give it strong weeknight appeal. The indoor/outdoor layout and welcoming approach to kids and dogs make it a standout for mixed-group visits.
policyNotes: Outside food permitted at your table (indoor and outdoor)
Dogs: dog park (off-leash) + leashed at tables + leashed inside tasting room if quiet
Food available Fri–Sun and Wed evenings on site
Children must remain within arm's reach of parent
Live music regularly scheduled — multiple events per week in season (see calendar)

wineries.name: The Vineyards & Winery at Lost Creek
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 100% Loudoun-grown wine served speakeasy-style in downtown Leesburg.
wineries.editorial: Lost Creek has relocated its public tasting experience from the vineyard to Echelon Wine Bar, a speakeasy-style space in downtown historic Leesburg. The wines are 100% Loudoun County-grown and pair well with a full dinner or brunch menu. Important caveat: the winery's vineyard on Spinks Ferry Road in Bluemont is a production facility only — it is not open to the public for visits.
policyNotes: Urban tasting room in downtown Leesburg — not a vineyard property
Dogs allowed on lawn area only
Food/culinary pairings on site; Chef's Tasting experience via Tock

wineries.name: Hillsborough Winery & Brewery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Wine and craft beer on the same property — accessible noon-to-8 schedule for western Loudoun.
wineries.editorial: Hillsborough combines a winery and brewery on the same Loudoun County property just outside Purcellville, making it a genuine two-for-one stop for wine and craft beer fans. The open daily noon-to-8pm schedule is among the most accessible in western Loudoun, and the pet-friendly policy is a draw for dog owners exploring Charles Town Pike wine country.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome leashed inside tasting room and on patio
On-site kitchen: salads, soups, brick-oven flatbreads
Live music every Friday 5–8 PM, April through October

wineries.name: Fabbioli Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Small family operation known for fruit wines alongside traditional varietals.
wineries.editorial: A small, family-owned operation on Limestone School Road in Leesburg, Fabbioli Cellars produces handcrafted wines — including notable fruit wines alongside traditional varietals — and runs a low-key, intimate tasting room experience. The closed Tuesday–Wednesday midweek schedule is typical for smaller Loudoun producers. Worth a stop for visitors exploring the eastern end of the Loudoun Wine Trail.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome leashed outdoors; must clean up
BYO food permitted outdoors (picnic area); NOT inside tasting room
Monthly curated tasting: 7 wines + gourmet food pairings from local chefs
Live music Saturdays — multiple performers per month

wineries.name: Three Fox Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Picnic on the lawn, off-leash dog in the meadow, weekend food trucks — Delaplane unhurried.
wineries.editorial: A Thursday-through-Sunday operation in the rolling Fauquier countryside near Delaplane, Three Fox leans into the picnic-on-the-lawn experience — bring your own lunch, let the dog run in the meadow, and settle in with a glass. Food trucks most weekends fill in the gaps. The abbreviated schedule means weekday visits aren't an option, but weekend afternoons here feel genuinely unhurried.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome indoors (except upstairs lounge) and outdoors; off-leash in meadow under direct supervision
BYO food and non-alcoholic beverages permitted inside and outside
Outside alcohol PROHIBITED anywhere on property
Children welcome everywhere including indoors, except upstairs lounge
Outdoor options: seasonal patio, year-round covered deck, vineyard seating, meadow bar (May–Oct weekends)
North and West views from deck
Food trucks most Saturdays and Sundays; prepackaged snacks available

wineries.name: Naked Mountain Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Pets inside the tasting room, outside food on the grounds — Fauquier's most welcoming all-around policy.
wineries.editorial: Sitting at the foot of the Blue Ridge in Markham, Naked Mountain has one of the most welcoming all-around policies of any Fauquier County winery — pets inside the tasting room, outside food on the grounds, children welcome, and no reservation required for most groups. The Saturday extended hours to 7 PM and the scenic Blue Ridge backdrop make it a strong weekend destination for multi-group visits.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome inside tasting room, on lawn, and on deck — leash required
BYO food permitted inside, on deck, and on grounds
No outside alcohol (Virginia ABC); only Naked Mountain wines on property
Children welcome anywhere on property under supervision
No reservation required for parties under 8
Food onsite: sandwiches, small plates, charcuterie (varies seasonally)

wineries.name: Horton Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Virginia wine pioneer — Viognier and Tannat before they were trendy. Daily 10 AM open.
wineries.editorial: Horton Vineyards near Gordonsville is a Virginia wine pioneer — founder Dennis Horton championed Viognier and Tannat in the Commonwealth before either variety was fashionable. The daily 10 AM schedule makes it one of the earlier-opening wineries in the state. Located along the Spotswood Trail in Orange County, it's a natural stop on any central Virginia wine route.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome inside and outside; treats and water bowls provided
Family-friendly with kids coloring table; hosts family events
Cafe on site with food available
BYO picnic food permitted on grounds
Live music concerts and events hosted regularly
Blue Ridge Mountain views from property

wineries.name: Prince Michel Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Multi-room estate winery with pub, on-site dining, and seven-day hours — easy walk-in stop on the 29 corridor.
wineries.editorial: Prince Michel is one of the oldest commercial wineries in the Madison/Orange corridor, with a multi-room facility that includes a tasting room, a pub room, and on-site accommodations. Self-guided tastings are walk-in friendly all week — a useful baseline when most Virginia wineries push reservations on weekends. The Mon evening (8 PM close) and Fri/Sat extended hours (9 PM close) give it strong dinner-pairing range that most rural wineries don't try to compete with.
policyNotes: Self-guided tour + tasting — no reservation required walk-in
Private tours and group experiences require advance booking (call or email)
Dogs welcome on the property — leashed (non-retractable) only; NOT inside the tasting room, pub room, or other indoor areas
Family-owned, family-friendly setting; on-site accommodations available
Mon evening close 8 PM; Fri/Sat close 9 PM; closed nights otherwise

wineries.name: Old House Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Multi-venue complex — winery, brewery, distillery, and Irish pub on one property.
wineries.editorial: Old House Vineyards in Culpeper has evolved into a multi-venue complex under the 'Old House Today' brand, incorporating a winery, brewery, distillery, and Irish pub on the same property. Different venues operate on different days, so arrival intent matters — the winery, brewery, and pub have distinct schedules and policies. The Friday extended hours and weekend food service make it the best time to experience the full offering.
policyNotes: Multiple venues on property: winery, brewery, distillery, Irish Pub — each with separate schedules
Irish Pub is 21+ only; other venues family-friendly
Dogs welcome outdoors only — must be leashed
BYO picnic food welcome; picnic tables available
75-acre property with Blue Ridge Mountain views and pond
Live music at seasonal celebrations and special events

wineries.name: Rappahannock Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Hot baguette sandwiches, dogs on the patio, BYO picnic after your tasting — daily noon open.
wineries.editorial: Set in the pastoral foothills of Rappahannock County near Huntly, Rappahannock Cellars is a genuinely relaxed daily operation with a welcoming policy toward kids, dogs, and picnickers. The hot baguette sandwiches made on-site are a cut above the typical charcuterie board, and the seven-days-a-week noon schedule makes it easy to incorporate into a weekend drive through the county.
policyNotes: Dogs AND cats welcome leashed in all outdoor areas; pet station + water/treats available
Light fare menu: cheeses, baguette sandwiches, spreads
Extensive outdoor seating: patios, decks, lawn, porches, pavilion, rooftop patio

wineries.name: Chatham Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Coastal Eastern Shore farm winery — actively encourages takeout picnics from local restaurants.
wineries.editorial: On the unspoiled Virginia Eastern Shore near Machipongo, Chatham Vineyards is one of the state's most distinctive wine destinations — estate-grown vines on a working farm with direct access to coastal breezes that define the wine's character. The winery actively encourages picnicking with takeout from local restaurants, and the daily 10 AM opening is among the earliest in the state.
policyNotes: BYO food from local restaurants actively encouraged — picnic on the grounds
Food onsite: local cheese, freshly baked bread, shareable snacks in tasting room
Outdoor iron tables for picnicking with Church Creek views
Live music events at the Crush Pad — no confirmed weekly cadence
Dogs welcome leashed inside tasting room, on porch/patio, and outside

wineries.name: Cross Keys Vineyards
wineries.address: 6011 E Timber Ridge Rd, Mt Crawford, VA 22841
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Panoramic Shenandoah views with an on-site bistro — open till 7 PM most nights.
wineries.editorial: Cross Keys Vineyards occupies a sweeping Rockingham County farm near Mt Crawford with panoramic Shenandoah Valley views and an on-site bistro that elevates it above most casual wine stops. The extended Monday–Saturday hours until 7 PM are among the latest in the valley. A reliable anchor for any Shenandoah Valley wine itinerary, particularly for those exploring the region south of Harrisonburg.
policyNotes: Outside food/picnics NOT permitted — on-site bistro
Dogs welcome leashed on outdoor patio and veranda; NOT inside
No age restriction; well-behaved kids welcome
Walk-ins up to 8; groups 8+ call ahead; 48-hr cancellation policy

wineries.name: Barrel Oak Winery & Brewery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 78-acre estate winery + brewery with sweeping Blue Ridge views — family AND dog friendly, with quiet 21+ zones.
wineries.editorial: Barrel Oak — "BOW" to regulars — sits on 78 acres in Delaplane's section of the Middleburg AVA, with a 30-acre estate vineyard and a side hustle in craft beer that's grown into a full brewery. Second-generation winemaker Jeremy Ligon brought home Gold at the 2026 Virginia Governor's Cup for the Meritage 2023 and Double Gold at the SF Chronicle Wine Competition for the Pinot Gris 2024. Family and dog friendly with quiet 21+ zones tucked in (Loft, Tasting Bars, fireplace seating); kids welcome everywhere else with direct adult supervision. Open daily — Mon–Thu noon to 6, Fri–Sun 11 to 7.
policyNotes: Open daily — Mon–Thu noon-6 PM, Fri–Sun 11 AM-7 PM
Reservations strongly recommended (required for groups of 9+)
Dogs welcome on leash on patios and grounds
Kids welcome with direct adult supervision (working farm)
21+ areas: Loft, Tasting Bars, Fireplace seating
BYO picnic at outdoor tables only — no outside alcohol per ABC regulations
Pizzas, charcuterie, rotating food trucks on site
Cellar tour + premier tasting available Dec–Aug — $40/person, by reservation
Award-winning: Gold at 2026 Virginia Governor's Cup (Meritage 2023)

wineries.name: Effingham Manor Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Upscale adults-only historic estate (circa 1767) with award-winning wines and chef's dinners.
wineries.editorial: Effingham Manor sits on a historic 1767 estate in Prince William County — Virginia's oldest continuously occupied home. The tasting room enforces a strict 21+ policy with no exceptions. No dogs, no kids, no outside food. What you get is an intimate, grown-up wine experience with regular chef's dinners, food trucks, and ladies' nights. The wines are solid and have earned Governor's Cup recognition.
policyNotes: 21+ ONLY — no persons under 21 permitted on the estate, no exceptions
No outside food or alcohol — Virginia ABC regulations
Walk-ins welcome, reservations recommended via Tock
Food trucks and chef's dinners on rotation

wineries.name: Nokesville Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Casual tasting room with trivia nights, fire pit patio, and community vibe.
wineries.editorial: Nokesville Winery is more neighborhood hangout than fancy estate. Thursday trivia at 7 PM draws a crowd, and the patio with fire pit is the move on cooler evenings. No reservations needed — just show up. They'll host private events up to 40 guests in the processing area. Silver medal winner at the 2024 Virginia Governor's Cup.
policyNotes: Pets welcome outside on patio only
2024 Virginia Governor's Cup Silver Medal winner

wineries.name: Private Label Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Boutique farm winery with hands-on winemaking experiences and tastings with the winemaker.
wineries.editorial: Private Label Cellars opened in late 2024, helmed by veteran Virginia winemaker Ashton Lough. This is as boutique as it gets — Fri–Sat only, noon to 6 PM. The draw is direct access to the winemaker and hands-on experiences like punch-downs during harvest and cork-opening classes. Double silver at the 2025 Virginia Governor's Cup for the 2021 Chardonnay and 2023 Cabernet Franc.
policyNotes: Open Friday & Saturday only, noon–6 PM
Hands-on experiences: punch-down, crush pad, cork class
2025 Virginia Governor's Cup double silver (Chardonnay, Cab Franc)

wineries.name: The Winery at Sunshine Ridge Farm
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Lakeside winery and brewery on Lake Manassas with wraparound porch and pergola seating.
wineries.editorial: Sunshine Ridge Farm overlooks Lake Manassas in Gainesville — one of the few lakeside winery settings in Northern Virginia. Both wine and beer on tap, plus multiple seating zones: plush couches inside, wraparound porch, and a pergola. Open late (until 9 PM Wed–Sat) and hosts private events and weddings. Part of the Steins, Vines & Moonshine Trail.
policyNotes: Part of the Steins, Vines & Moonshine Trail
Closed Tuesdays; open Mon & Sun noon–7 PM, Wed–Sat noon–9 PM

wineries.name: Walsh Family Wine
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-friendly estate winery with direct expression of Loudoun terroir.
wineries.editorial: Walsh Family Wine took over the former North Gate Vineyard property and brought a family-friendly, approachable vibe. Open daily noon–6 (Fridays until 8), no reservations needed for small groups. The focus is on authentic Virginia wines that express their Loudoun County vineyard sites. Private events and weddings available.
policyNotes: Open daily noon–6 PM, Fridays until 8 PM

wineries.name: Sunset Hills Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Former Amish farm with spectacular sunsets, mountain views, and a 21+ only policy.
wineries.editorial: Sunset Hills occupies a former Amish farm with a restored barn surrounded by vineyards. The property enforces a strict 21+ policy — no exceptions, entire property. Dogs welcome outdoors on leash (decks, lawns, Stone Pavilion) but not inside. Outside food allowed on porches and lawn but not in tasting room. Late Saturday hours until 8 PM for sunset views.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome outdoors on leash (decks, lawns, Stone Pavilion)
No dogs inside except service animals
No outside food in tasting room — lite fare menu available
BYO picnic OK on porches, Stone Pavilion, lawn (no hot foods or large catered platters)
Former Amish farm with restored barn

wineries.name: Willowcroft Farm Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Loudoun's oldest winery atop Mt. Gilead with Blue Ridge views since 1981.
wineries.editorial: Willowcroft is Loudoun County's OG — the first acre of vineyards planted in 1981, making it the oldest winery in the county. Perched atop Mt. Gilead with views of the distant Blue Ridge, it's a throwback to pre-boom Virginia wine. Dog and family-friendly. Outside food welcome (no outside alcohol). Open Thu–Sun.
policyNotes: Outside food welcome — no outside alcohol
Loudoun County's oldest winery — first vines planted 1981
Blue Ridge mountain views from Mt. Gilead

wineries.name: Hidden Brook Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Weekend-only boutique winery with intimate tastings in Leesburg.
wineries.editorial: Hidden Brook keeps it simple — Saturdays and Sundays only, no reservations needed. A small boutique operation in Leesburg that closes early about once a month for private events, so check before you go. Low-key alternative to the bigger Loudoun producers.
policyNotes: Weekend only — Sat 11:30 AM–6 PM, Sun noon–5 PM

wineries.name: Delaplane Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Intimate Fauquier winery with terrace seating and grass lawn for leashed dogs.
wineries.editorial: Delaplane Cellars sits on Winchester Road in the heart of Fauquier wine country. Open daily with slightly longer hours Fri–Sun. Dogs welcome but only in outdoor grass areas — not on the terrace or patio. Reservations via Tock for larger groups.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome in outdoor grass areas only
No dogs on terrace, patio, or in tasting room

wineries.name: RdV Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Ultra-premium by-appointment-only estate producing Virginia's most acclaimed Bordeaux blends.
wineries.editorial: RdV is Virginia's prestige play — Bordeaux-style blends that have earned national recognition and prices to match. Appointment only, no walk-ins, max party of 4. Open Thu–Sun. This is not a casual afternoon; it's a curated wine experience for serious enthusiasts willing to book ahead and pay up.

wineries.name: Blue Valley Vineyard and Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family and dog friendly estate with rolling Fauquier hills and extended weekend hours.
wineries.editorial: Blue Valley is the family-friendly play in Delaplane wine country. Dogs on leash? Welcome. Kids? Also welcome. Open daily with late Friday-Saturday hours until 7:30 PM. Wedding and event venue on the side. Easy atmosphere without the stuffiness of some neighboring estates.
policyNotes: Dog friendly — leashed dogs welcome on grounds

wineries.name: Narmada Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-owned Rappahannock winery blending Virginia terroir with Indian heritage.
wineries.editorial: Narmada brings a unique perspective to Virginia wine — founded by the Panicker family, the winery blends traditional winemaking with influences from India's Narmada River region. Open Thu–Mon, noon to 5 PM. Award-winning wines in a setting that feels more personal than corporate.

wineries.name: Pippin Hill Farm & Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Culinary-focused vineyard with farm-to-table dining and Blue Ridge views.
wineries.editorial: Pippin Hill is the culinary destination on the Monticello Wine Trail — farm-to-table dining that rivals standalone restaurants, paired with estate wines. 20 minutes south of Charlottesville. Dogs welcome on leash on lawn and veranda. Reservations via Resy recommended for dining. Closed Mondays.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome on leash on lawn and veranda

wineries.name: The Winery at Kindred Pointe
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Woman-owned winery and cidery on 58 scenic Shenandoah acres.
wineries.editorial: Kindred Pointe is a woman-owned operation on 58 acres in the heart of the Shenandoah Valley, just 5 miles off I-81. Wine and hard cider both on tap. Open daily noon–6 PM.

wineries.name: Stinson Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-run boutique winery in a repurposed garage with B&B.
wineries.editorial: Stinson is a family-run boutique winery in Crozet at the Blue Ridge foothills. The tasting room is a repurposed garage. B&B on property.

wineries.name: Ox-Eye Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Downtown Staunton tasting room with estate-grown wines.
wineries.editorial: Ox-Eye runs a tasting room in downtown Staunton — walkable from shops and restaurants. Estate-grown wines from their farm.

wineries.name: Otium Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 21+ only Tranquility Farm winery open Fri–Sun with estate wines and pastoral views.

wineries.editorial: Notaviva is the real deal — a family farm operation since 2008, expanded to include brewing in 2019. Friday night bluegrass jam is the signature event. 21+ ONLY venue. Dogs welcome outside on leash. BYO food allowed.

wineries.name: Tarara Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Potomac River bluffs winery with summer concert series.

wineries.name: Doukénie Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Award-winning Loudoun winery with 21+ tasting room and family-friendly outdoor gazebo.

policyNotes: NO DOGS — working farm with sheep and cattle

wineries.name: Petit Domaine Sparkling Winery

wineries.name: The Barns at Hamilton Station Vineyards

wineries.name: Gray Ghost Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Civil War-themed Amissville winery with picnic grounds and weekend hours.

wineries.name: Philip Carter Winery

wineries.name: Domaine Fortier Vineyards

wineries.name: Endhardt Vineyards

wineries.vibeDescriptor: Popular cider taproom on Route 151.
wineries.editorial: Bold Rock is a popular cidery on Route 151. Family-friendly with kids menu and sparkling sweet cider for non-drinkers. Pet-friendly venue. BYO picnic welcome inside or on decks/terraces. Reservations available by calling.
policyNotes: BYO picnic welcome inside or on decks

wineries.name: Blue Mountain Brewery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Popular brewery with great food and family vibe.
wineries.editorial: Blue Mountain is a beloved brewery on Route 151 with great food. Very family-friendly with a full kids menu. Dogs in pet-friendly outdoor section only (leashed). Full restaurant on-site. Reservations recommended for large parties.
policyNotes: Dogs in pet-friendly outdoor section only

wineries.name: Devils Backbone Brewing Company
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Award-winning brewery with outdoor meadows.
wineries.editorial: Devils Backbone is an award-winning Virginia brewery. Outdoor areas perfect for kids with non-alcoholic options. Dogs must stay leashed in designated pet area in The Meadows. Full restaurant on-site. Reservations recommended for weekends.
policyNotes: Dogs in designated pet area in The Meadows only

wineries.name: Hazy Mountain Vineyards & Brewery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-friendly winery and brewery combo.
wineries.editorial: Hazy Mountain is a family-friendly vineyard AND brewery. Dogs OUTDOOR ONLY on umbrella patio (leashed) — not in tasting room or covered patio. NO outside food (desserts from approved bakeries may be allowed). Reservations recommended for indoor/covered seating. Groups 14+ email ahead.
policyNotes: Dogs OUTDOOR umbrella patio only — not inside or covered patio

wineries.name: Barren Ridge Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-friendly Shenandoah Valley winery.
wineries.editorial: Barren Ridge is a family-friendly Shenandoah Valley winery. Dogs welcome indoors AND outdoors on leash (not during ticketed events). BYO food and drinks welcome. Groups 8+ call 24 hours ahead.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome inside AND outside on leash
Dogs NOT allowed during ticketed events

wineries.name: CrossKeys Vineyards
wineries.address: 6011 E. Timber Ridge Rd, Mt. Crawford, VA 22841
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Shenandoah Valley estate with on-site bistro.
wineries.editorial: CrossKeys is a beautiful estate with an on-site bistro. Kids welcome. Dogs allowed on outside patio and veranda only (leashed) — NOT inside. NO outside food — bistro on-site. Bistro reservations strongly recommended.
policyNotes: Dogs on patio/veranda only — not inside

wineries.name: North Mountain Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Child-friendly with dogs inside.
wineries.editorial: North Mountain is child-friendly with families welcome. Pet-friendly — dogs allowed in tasting room. BYO picnic welcome — light fare also available. Groups 10+ contact ahead. Open Wed–Sun.

wineries.name: Wisteria Farm & Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Working farm winery with play area and sheep.
wineries.editorial: Wisteria is a working farm with Romney sheep and chickens. Family-friendly with play area for children. Pets welcome on leash. BYO picnic by the creek welcome (no outside alcohol). Groups 8+ call ahead. Farm animals are not pets — do not feed or chase.
policyNotes: BYO picnic by the creek — no outside alcohol
Working farm with sheep and chickens
Groups 8+ call ahead; 10+ space rental fee

wineries.name: James River Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Richmond-area winery with dogs inside.
wineries.editorial: James River Cellars is a popular Richmond-area winery. Family-friendly — children must stay at their table. Dogs welcome indoors and outdoors (leashed) — not on upper deck. BYO food welcome. Groups 10+ should make reservations.
policyNotes: Children must stay at their table
Dogs inside and outside on leash — not on upper deck

wineries.name: Grayhaven Winery
wineries.address: 4675 E Grey Fox Circle, Gum Spring, VA 23065
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family winery with koi pond and horses.
wineries.editorial: Grayhaven is a family-friendly winery with a koi pond and horses to see. Non-alcoholic drinks for kids. Dog-friendly outdoors — water bowls provided. BYO picnic welcome — cheese/charcuterie also available.
policyNotes: Family-friendly — koi pond and horses to see

wineries.name: New Kent Winery
wineries.address: 8400 Old Church Road, New Kent, VA 23124
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Winery and brewery between Richmond and Williamsburg.
wineries.editorial: New Kent Winery includes Talleysville Brewing. Families welcome — children must be supervised. Dogs on patios and green space during business hours only (leashed) — not in tasting room or during concerts. NO outside food or beverages. Groups 8+ contact in advance.
policyNotes: Dogs on patios/green space during business hours only — not in tasting room

wineries.name: Saude Creek Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: New Kent winery with picnic grounds.
wineries.editorial: Saude Creek welcomes families — children must stay with parents. Under 21 cannot drink even with parental consent. Dogs in designated pet areas outdoors only (leashed); service animals only indoors. BYO picnic permitted — no large rolling coolers. Groups 15+ must reserve.
policyNotes: Under 21 cannot drink even with parental consent
Dogs in designated outdoor areas only
BYO picnic — no large rolling coolers

wineries.name: Upper Shirley Vineyards
wineries.address: 600 Shirley Plantation Road, Charles City, VA 23030
wineries.vibeDescriptor: James River plantation winery with restaurant.
wineries.editorial: Upper Shirley is set on historic Shirley Plantation along the James River. Children allowed — family-friendly. NO PETS allowed on property (strict policy). NO outside food or beverages by law — restaurant on-site. Reservations via OpenTable recommended.
policyNotes: NO outside food or beverages — by law
Restaurant on-site — food service until 4 PM

wineries.name: Gauthier Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 21+ tasting room with brick oven pizza.
wineries.editorial: Gauthier has a STRICT age policy: Under 21 NOT permitted in tasting room (including infants). Must remain within arm's reach on property. Dogs on porch/deck/patios only (not in tasting room). Brick oven pizza restaurant on-site. Groups 7+ require 48-hour advance notice.
policyNotes: Under 21 NOT permitted in tasting room (including infants)
Must remain within arm's reach on property
Dogs on porch/deck/patios only — not in tasting room

wineries.name: The Williamsburg Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Virginia's largest winery with restaurant and events.
wineries.editorial: Virginia's flagship winery with Gabriel Archer Tavern on-site. Kids 12 and under must be supervised. UPPER LEVEL of Wine Pavilion is 21+ ONLY; lower deck is all-ages. Dogs on patio and lawn near Wine Pavilion only — NOT inside tasting room, restaurant, or covered deck. NO outside food allowed.
policyNotes: Kids 12 and under must be supervised
Dogs on patio/lawn only — NOT inside

wineries.name: Silver Hand Meadery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Craft meadery in downtown Williamsburg.
wineries.editorial: Unique meadery in Williamsburg. Mead tastings are 21+ with valid ID. Honey tastings are ALL AGES. Kids allowed with small snacks. Dogs on outdoor patio only (leashed); service dogs inside.

wineries.name: Mermaid Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Urban winery and restaurant in downtown Norfolk.
wineries.editorial: Urban winery with full restaurant in downtown Norfolk. Also has a Virginia Beach location. Families welcome — kid menu available. NO outside food (full-service restaurant). Reservations recommended.

wineries.name: Virginia Beach Winery
wineries.address: 1064 Lynnhaven Parkway, Suite 110, Virginia Beach, VA 23452
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Casual neighborhood winery near Virginia Beach.
wineries.editorial: Relaxed winery in Virginia Beach. Family-friendly atmosphere. BYO food allowed — bring food from nearby restaurants. $5 daily wine tasting. Walk-ins welcome.

wineries.name: SummerWind Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Dog-friendly vineyard near Smithfield.
wineries.editorial: Family and dog-friendly vineyard with dog-friendly grassy area. Outside food NOT allowed inside — BUT can enjoy in grass/picnic area. Charcuterie available. Reservations recommended for parties of 6+.
policyNotes: Outside food in picnic area only

wineries.name: Hampton Roads Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Working farm winery with goat tower attraction.
wineries.editorial: Family-friendly farm winery. Dogs allowed inside AND outside — must be leashed and friendly. Features 'World's Tallest Goat Tower' attraction. BYO picnic welcome. Walk-ins welcome for groups under 8.

wineries.name: Waters Edge Winery and Bistro
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Urban winery with full bistro menu.
wineries.editorial: Urban winery and bistro in Norfolk. Family-friendly — kid menu available. Dog-friendly. NO outside food (full bistro menu). Reservations strongly recommended.

wineries.name: Breezy Hill Meadworks
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Craft meadery with Mead Hall tasting room.
wineries.editorial: Craft meadery in Isle of Wight County. Leashed pets welcome. Mead Hall with indoor and patio seating. Also features candles, soaps and bee products. Weekend hours only.

wineries.name: Villa Appalaccia Winery
wineries.address: 752 Rock Castle Gorge Road, Floyd, VA 24091
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Italian-style winery on Blue Ridge Parkway.
wineries.editorial: Beautiful Italian-style winery near Blue Ridge Parkway. 'We love kids' — family-friendly. Leashed, friendly dogs welcome. BYO food welcome — NO outside alcohol. Walk-ins welcome.
policyNotes: BYO food welcome — NO outside alcohol

wineries.name: Beliveau Farm Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Dual tasting room winery near Blacksburg.
wineries.editorial: Beliveau has TWO tasting rooms: one pet-friendly and one 21+ only (no pets). Dogs allowed OUTDOORS ONLY — must be leashed. BYO picnic food during regular hours (not special events). No Uber/Lyft service — bring a designated driver.
policyNotes: Two tasting rooms: pet-friendly OR 21+ no pets
Dogs OUTDOORS ONLY — must be leashed

wineries.name: Attimo Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Pet-friendly Christiansburg winery.
wineries.editorial: Pet-friendly winery in Christiansburg. Kids allowed. Picnic area available. $5-$10 tasting fee.

wineries.name: The New River Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Virginia's first certified craft winery.
wineries.editorial: Virginia's first certified craft winery. Friendly, leashed dogs welcome in tasting room. Child-friendly with picnic area. Reservations recommended for 6+ (limited to 1.5 hours). Delivery and shipping within Virginia available.
policyNotes: Dogs welcome in tasting room (friendly, leashed)

wineries.name: West Wind Farm Vineyard & Winery
wineries.address: 180 W Wind Drive, Max Meadows, VA 24360
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family winery near I-81 in Wythe County.
wineries.editorial: Family winery near I-81. Well-behaved dogs allowed in tasting room, lawn, and patio. Kid-friendly. BYO picnic welcome — picnic benches available. Walk-ins welcome.
policyNotes: Dogs in tasting room, lawn, patio

wineries.name: Iron Heart Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Small family winery with resident cat and dogs.
wineries.editorial: Small family winery. Well-behaved, leashed dogs welcome indoors and outdoors — winery cat and dogs may greet you. Family-friendly atmosphere. Weekend hours only.

wineries.name: Peaks of Otter Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 6th generation family farm winery.
wineries.editorial: 6th generation family farm. Very pet and child-friendly — farm animals to visit. Dogs welcome inside and outside on leash. BYO food welcome. 3 tastings free, $5 for more (keep souvenir glass). Groups 20+ should give heads up.
policyNotes: Dogs inside and outside on leash

wineries.name: Virginia Mountain Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Mountain winery with games and picnic area.
wineries.editorial: Dogs welcome inside for tasting OR outside on porch/vineyard tables. Kids welcome — games available (ping pong, foosball, cornhole). Bring a blanket for picnics. Reservations recommended for 4+ guests. Open March-December.
policyNotes: Games for kids (ping pong, foosball, cornhole)

wineries.name: Stoney Brook Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family winery with Sipping Porch.
wineries.editorial: Family winery. Dogs on Sipping Porch and farm areas ONLY — must be leashed, friendly. Kid-friendly. BYO food welcome — chips, cheese boxes available. Weekend hours only.
policyNotes: Dogs on Sipping Porch and farm areas only

wineries.name: Hamlet Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Sunday-only winery near Smith River.
wineries.editorial: Henry County winery open SUNDAYS ONLY year-round. Dogs on Tasting Terrace only — must be leashed. Kids allowed but must be supervised (small pond on property). NO outside food or alcohol. Reservations HIGHLY RECOMMENDED, required for groups 11+.
policyNotes: Kids must be supervised — pond on property

wineries.name: General's Ridge Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Award-winning winery with lodging options.
wineries.editorial: Award-winning winery owned by Major General Rick Phillips USMC (Ret.). Dogs allowed inside. Family-friendly. Live music events. Lodging available with large rental homes overlooking vineyards. Wheelchair accessible.

wineries.name: Rivah Vineyards at The Grove
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Historic 125-acre family estate since 1799.
wineries.editorial: 7th generation Taylor family ownership on 125-acre estate. Pet-friendly — bring kids and pets. Riverside deck access and fire pit seating. Wedding and event venue. $8 tasting with glass, $6 without.

wineries.name: The Hague Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Small family winery on Historic Buena Vista Plantation.
wineries.editorial: Small family winery on 1835 historic plantation. Tasting room in former barn. Pet-friendly. Child-friendly. Picnic area available. $6 tasting fee. French-style wines.

wineries.name: Monroe Bay Winery
wineries.address: 4786 James Monroe Highway, Colonial Beach, VA 22443
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Waterfront winery on James Monroe birthplace land.
wineries.editorial: Small farm winery and cidery on Monroe Creek waterfront. Pets allowed — shaded outdoor area. Family-friendly. BYO picnic or snack — food trucks announced on Facebook. Groups 10+ need advance contact. Open April-December only.

wineries.name: Jacey Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 150-acre waterfront estate accessible by boat.
wineries.editorial: 150-acre waterfront parcel on Mill Creek — accessible by boat (3 private docks). Full tapas menu available. Villas available for rental. Wedding venue. Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail.
policyNotes: Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail

wineries.name: Ditchley Cider Works & Farm
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Historic 162-acre cidery with manor house from 1688.
wineries.editorial: Veteran-owned cidery on 162-acre historic property. Dogs on grounds ONLY — not in buildings (well-behaved, leashed). Child-friendly. Manor house tours $10. Groups 6+ highly recommended to reserve. Closed Jan-Feb.
policyNotes: Dogs on grounds only — not in buildings

wineries.name: Good Luck Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Community-based vineyard with dog patrol squad.
wineries.editorial: Community-based vineyard on 100-acre estate. Friendly, leashed dogs on porch and outdoor space ONLY — NOT indoors, keep out of vineyard. Children welcome. BYO food welcome — NO outside alcohol (strictly enforced). Groups 8+ call ahead. Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail.
policyNotes: Dogs on porch/outdoors only — NOT indoors
Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail

wineries.name: The Dog and Oyster Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: America's only vineyard crafting wines to pair with oysters.
wineries.editorial: Micro-vineyard at Hope and Glory Inn — America's only vineyard crafting wines to pair with oysters. Named for rescue dogs that protect grapes. Dog-friendly. Upscale oyster bar. Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail.
policyNotes: Part of Hope and Glory Inn
Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail

wineries.name: Caret Cellars
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Family-owned Virginia Farm Winery with Italian flair.
wineries.editorial: Family-owned farm winery with Italian influence. 6.5-acre vineyard with 12 wine varieties. Dog-friendly. Child-friendly. Hand-harvested grapes. Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail.
policyNotes: Part of Chesapeake Bay Wine Trail

wineries.name: Wind Vineyards at Laurel Grove
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Largest farm winery in Eastern Virginia - 700 acres.
wineries.editorial: Eastern Virginia's largest farm winery on 700-acre farm. 25 grape varieties. Gold Medal at Virginia Governor's Cup. Monster truck shows, live music, pick-your-own sunflowers. Deadrise Kitchen on-site. Family-friendly destination.
policyNotes: Largest farm winery in Eastern Virginia

wineries.name: Zoll Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Gloucester County's first winery - farm-to-table.
wineries.editorial: Gloucester County's first winery. 16.5-acre farm-to-table estate. Owned by pastry chef Frank Zoll (former Tavern on the Green). Pet-friendly. Child-friendly. Live music, comedy shows, art classes. $16 tasting, free tours. Reservations recommended.

wineries.name: Rosemont of Virginia Vineyards & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 450-acre estate near Lake Gaston.
wineries.editorial: 450-acre estate near Lake Gaston on VA/NC border. 100% estate-grown wines from 22 acres. Dogs on side porches and lawn areas. Family-friendly. BYO picnic welcome — no outside alcohol. $10-$15 flight.

wineries.name: Hunting Creek Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Small family vineyard with Barn event venue.
wineries.editorial: Small family vineyard with The Barn event venue. Dogs welcome. Kids welcome. Snacks, cheese, meat trays available. Flights $1.50-$13.50. Weekend hours — appointments available other times.

wineries.name: Bright Meadows Farm Vineyard & Winery
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Very pet-friendly farm winery.
wineries.editorial: Very pet-friendly farm winery. Dogs allowed inside and in large picnic area — 3/4 mile trail, dogs can swim in pond. Kids welcome (10 and under free at events). BYO picnic encouraged. $5 tasting fee. Weekend walk-in, Tue-Thu by appointment.
policyNotes: Dogs inside and outside — swimming pond, trail

wineries.name: Woodbine Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Barn tasting room with reservable wine stalls.
wineries.editorial: Barn tasting room with 6 reservable 'wine stalls.' Pets welcome — must be leashed. Children welcome but must be supervised (pond on property). BYO picnic welcome — charcuterie boxes available. NO outside alcohol. $15 tasting for 3 flight options.

wineries.name: The Homeplace Vineyard
wineries.vibeDescriptor: Chatham winery with Flip Flop Fridays.
wineries.editorial: Family winery in Chatham. Non-aggressive, leashed dogs allowed. Children must be supervised. BYO food allowed (coolers inspected) — NO outside alcohol. Groups 8+ call ahead. Flip Flop Fridays with food, live music.
policyNotes: Flip Flop Fridays with live music

wineries.name: DeVault Family Vineyards
wineries.vibeDescriptor: 32-acre family farm with activities.
wineries.editorial: 32-acre family farm winery. Family-friendly with small animals, wagon rides. Tennis court, volleyball, basketball, stocked pond, indoor pool. Weekend hours only.
